subject.purpose: checks tree plan files against the grammar
subject.reader: the tree skill's author, whose owner sees a broken page when a malformed plan passes

promises.text: prints "ok N", or one error per line and exits 1
prints a line per refused file, then "refused K of N"

flaws: a stack trace hides which file was wrong
a rule the author cannot look up

criteria.text: Run on a valid plan file, the script prints `ok 1` and exits 0.
criteria.from: ISO/IEC 25010 functional correctness: the verdict is right

criteria.text: Run on a plan with an unknown key, the script exits 1 with the rule name `unknown-key` in its output.
criteria.from: ISO/IEC 25010 functional correctness: the verdict is right
criteria.command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 check-plan.py refused/written-id.json | grep unknown-key; ! PYTHONPATH=. python3 check-plan.py refused/written-id.json >/dev/null
criteria.fix: Refuse a key the grammar lacks.

criteria.text: Run on a plan file that writes one key twice in an object, the script exits 1 and prints the rule name `duplicate-key`.
criteria.from: ISO/IEC 25010 functional correctness: the verdict is right
criteria.command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 check-plan.py refused/two-picks.json | grep duplicate-key; ! PYTHONPATH=. python3 check-plan.py refused/two-picks.json >/dev/null
criteria.fix: Refuse a repeated key when the file loads.

criteria.text: An `evidence` part that lacks a source draws exit 1 and `evidence-needs-source`.
criteria.from: ISO/IEC 25010 functional correctness: the verdict is right
criteria.command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 check-plan.py refused/evidence-without-source.json | grep evidence-needs-source; ! PYTHONPATH=. python3 check-plan.py refused/evidence-without-source.json >/dev/null

criteria.text: Run with no argument, the script exits 2, prints nothing on stdout and prints its docstring on stderr.
criteria.command: out=$(PYTHONPATH=. python3 check-plan.py 2>/dev/null); status=$?; test $status -eq 2 && test -z "$out" && PYTHONPATH=. python3 check-plan.py 2>&1 | grep '^usage:'
criteria.fix: Print the docstring on stderr and exit 2.

criteria.text: Run on a path that does not exist, the script exits 1 and prints a line holding `unreadable`, with no `Traceback` on stderr.
criteria.from: ISO/IEC 25010 fault tolerance: a bad input fails in form
criteria.command: out=$(PYTHONPATH=. python3 check-plan.py refused/none.json 2>&1); status=$?; echo "$out"; test $status -eq 1 && echo "$out" | grep -q unreadable && ! echo "$out" | grep -q Traceback
criteria.fix: Report an unreadable file as a rule.

criteria.text: Run on a file of invalid UTF-8 bytes, the script exits 1 with an error line and no `Traceback` on stderr.
criteria.from: ISO/IEC 25010 fault tolerance: a bad input fails in form
criteria.command: out=$(PYTHONPATH=. python3 check-plan.py refused/not-utf8.json 2>&1); status=$?; echo "$out" | tail -1; test $status -eq 1 && ! echo "$out" | grep -q Traceback
criteria.fix: Catch UnicodeDecodeError in errors_of as an unreadable file.

criteria.text: Run with `--expect-refused` on one refused plan file, the script prints a last line `refused 1 of 1` and exits 0.
criteria.from: ISO/IEC 25010 functional correctness: the verdict is right
criteria.command: PYTHONPATH=. python3 check-plan.py --expect-refused refused/written-id.json | tail -1 | grep -x 'refused 1 of 1'
criteria.fix: End the run with the refused count.

criteria.text: The script's docstring opens with a purpose sentence and holds one `usage:` line per call form.
criteria.command: sed -n 2p check-plan.py | grep -q '[.]$' && grep -cE '^(usage: |       )check-plan.py ' check-plan.py | grep -x 2
criteria.fix: Open the docstring with a purpose and give a usage line per call.

criteria.text: The script defines `def main(args)` and ends with `sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))`.
criteria.command: grep -q '^def main(args):' check-plan.py && tail -1 check-plan.py | grep -F 'sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))'
criteria.fix: Use the main form of AGENTS.md.

criteria.text: Each rule name that `tree_plan.check` can emit appears in the tree skill's `references/grammar.md`.
criteria.command: ! grep -oE '"[a-z]+(-[a-z]+)+"' tree_plan.py | tr -d '"' | sort -u | while read -r rule; do grep -qF "$rule" grammar.txt || echo "undocumented: $rule"; done | grep undocumented
criteria.fix: Add each undocumented rule to the grammar.

criteria.text: `tree_plan.py` opens a file only in `load_file` and imports no network module.
criteria.from: the lib's docstring: every function is a calculation

criteria.text: Each comment in either file says why, not what the next line does.
criteria.anchors: Says why: removing the comment loses a reason, not a paraphrase of the code line. List one item per comment.
